entries.concept: Python FastAPI multi-stage Dockerfile with non-root user and health check
entries.description: Two-stage Python production Dockerfile: builder stage (python:3.11-slim) installs packages with pip install --no-cache-dir --user, runtime stage (python:3.11-slim) creates non-root appuser (UID 1001), copies /root/.local from builder, sets PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1, adds HEALTHCHECK with httpx, exposes 8000. CMD: uvicorn with --workers 1 --no-access-log.
decision_rules: Use --user flag in pip install to install to /root/.local, then copy to the runtime user's home
Set PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 to skip .pyc file generation in the runtime image
Add HEALTHCHECK with initialDelaySeconds=40s to accommodate application startup time
tradeoffs: Runtime stage still uses python:3.11-slim (not distroless) to allow httpx for health check — use distroless if health check is done via external probe
anti_patterns: Installing dependencies in the runtime stage — defeats the multi-stage cache benefit
Running uvicorn with multiple workers behind a container orchestrator — use 1 worker per container and scale horizontally
aws_alignment: Map HEALTHCHECK to ECS container health check for load balancer target group deregistration

entries.concept: Node.js multi-stage Dockerfile with npm ci and non-root user
entries.description: Two-stage Node.js Dockerfile: builder stage (node:20-alpine) runs npm ci --only=production and npm run build, runtime stage (node:20-alpine) creates non-root appuser (UID 1001), copies dist and node_modules with --chown, adds HEALTHCHECK with wget, exposes 3000. CMD: node dist/server.js.
decision_rules: Use npm ci (not npm install) in builder stage — deterministic install from package-lock.json
Use --only=production in npm ci to exclude devDependencies from the runtime image
Use alpine variant to minimize image size
tradeoffs: Alpine uses musl libc — some native Node.js addons may have compatibility issues; use debian-slim variants if needed
anti_patterns: Using npm install instead of npm ci — non-deterministic and slower
Copying node_modules from host into the image — includes devDependencies and platform-specific binaries

entries.concept: Java Spring Boot multi-stage Dockerfile with layer extraction
entries.description: Two-stage Spring Boot Dockerfile: builder stage (maven:3.9-eclipse-temurin-17) runs mvn dependency:go-offline -B to cache deps, then mvn package -DskipTests -B. Runtime stage (eclipse-temurin:17-jre-alpine) creates non-root appuser, runs java -Djarmode=layertools -jar app.jar extract to split JAR into layers for better Docker caching, adds HEALTHCHECK with wget on /actuator/health. JVM options: -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75.0, -XX:+UseContainerSupport.
decision_rules: Run mvn dependency:go-offline before copying src — creates a cacheable layer for Maven dependencies
Use -Djarmode=layertools to extract Spring Boot layers for optimized Docker caching on partial rebuilds
Use -XX:UseContainerSupport and -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75.0 for proper JVM memory management in containers
tradeoffs: Layer extraction increases build steps but significantly reduces rebuild time when only application code changes
anti_patterns: Copying all Maven dependencies into the final image — use the JRE runtime stage only
Not setting -XX:UseContainerSupport — JVM may use host memory limits instead of container limits, causing OOMKills
aws_alignment: Set JVM MaxRAMPercentage to leave headroom for the container memory limit overhead in ECS/EKS

entries.description: Exclude from Docker build context: version control (.git/, .gitignore, .gitattributes), secrets (.env, .env.*, *.pem, *.key, *.p12, *.pfx, secrets/), Python artifacts (__pycache__/, *.pyc, .venv/, dist/, .pytest_cache/, .mypy_cache/, htmlcov/), Node artifacts (node_modules/, npm-debug.log, .npm/), Docker files (Dockerfile*, docker-compose*, .dockerignore), IDE files (.idea/, .vscode/, .DS_Store), CI/CD files (.github/, Jenkinsfile), docs (docs/, *.md), tests (tests/, test/, spec/).
decision_rules: Always include a .dockerignore in every project that has a Dockerfile
Exclude .env* patterns to prevent accidental secret inclusion in build context
Exclude tests/ to keep production images smaller
tradeoffs: Excluding Dockerfile and docker-compose files from context is safe but may complicate multi-stage builds that copy compose files — adjust as needed
anti_patterns: Not having a .dockerignore — entire repository including secrets is sent to Docker daemon

entries.description: Optimize Docker build cache by separating frequently changing layers from stable layers. Pattern: COPY requirements.txt . (stable — cache hit), RUN pip install -r requirements.txt (cached unless requirements change), COPY . . (frequently changing — always invalidates). The wrong pattern copies all source before installing, invalidating the pip install cache on every code change.
decision_rules: Always copy dependency manifests (requirements.txt, package.json, pom.xml) before copying source code
Place COPY . . as late as possible in the Dockerfile to maximize cache reuse of earlier layers
tradeoffs: Separate dependency and source COPY instructions add a line to the Dockerfile but dramatically reduce CI build times
anti_patterns: COPY . . followed by RUN pip install — invalidates pip cache on every code change
Combining dependency installation and source copy in a single RUN — prevents cache layering
aws_alignment: Use GitHub Actions cache with type=gha for Docker BuildKit layer caching in CI (cache-from/cache-to gha)
